text:
Sampled evaluation can change model ordering: uniform and popularity-based candidate sets both produced rankings inconsistent with full-catalog evaluation in sequential recommendation ([Dallmann et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045)). More recent evidence shows aggregate accuracy can hide head/mid/tail imbalances; random training negatives favored head items, while popularity-based negatives sometimes improved balance at an accuracy cost ([Prakash et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276)). A 2025 study further treats sampling reliability as dependent on sampling strategy and data conditions ([RecSys paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086)). Large training margins therefore do not establish generalization or full-catalog ranking quality.

Suggested diagnostic synthesis: freeze training-prefix/next-item pairs and candidate identities across checkpoints; construct separate uniform, training-frequency-matched, and title/description lexical-hard panels. Exclude prefix-seen items and the positive from distractors, deduplicate, and treat unobserved distractors as potentially relevant. Report positive rank, percentile rank, pairwise win rate, and head/mid/tail breakdowns. Track both positive-to-10th-distractor gaps and candidate-list 10th–11th score gaps, normalized by within-panel score dispersion; raw margins vary with score scale. Ranks survive strictly increasing score transformations, while normalized gaps survive positive affine rescaling only. Measure top-10 overlap across checkpoints and repeated fixed panels. These are proposed probes, not a validated diagnostic package from the cited papers.

Compare checkpoint-level probe changes with available host validation HR@10 separately per category and by the four-category macro-average; no outcomes were supplied here to establish agreement. Keep the pinned evaluator unchanged. For the twenty designated users, report full-catalog unseen-item exposure through catalog coverage, recommendation concentration, popularity distribution, and list overlap. Those describe exposure, not relevance accuracy, and should remain separate from sampled HR@10.
